messages.subject: Extract details on Pareto K after fitting a model
messages.subject_clean: Extract details on Pareto K after fitting a model
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
thanks for the great package and the help forum.

When fitting models I often experience high Pareto ks. How can I extract information for Pareto k, other than the warning that is displayed?

 I would like to get something like this as available from the standard Stan code:

Computed from 12000 by 20 log-likelihood matrix Estimate SE elpd_loo -1875.5 83.0 p_loo 32.6 2.0 looic 3751.0 166.0 ------ Monte Carlo SE of elpd_loo is NA. Pareto k diagnostic values: Count Pct. Min. n_eff (-Inf, 0.5] (good) 0 0.0% <NA> (0.5, 0.7] (ok) 0 0.0% <NA> (0.7, 1] (bad) 16 80.0% 21 (1, Inf) (very bad) 4 20.0% 9 See help('pareto-k-diagnostic') for details.

I might be obvious, but I seem to be unable to extract these bits of information.
thanks a lot!
Franziska

messages.body_plain:
Hi Franziska,

You can utilize the 'extract_ic' function to get the Pareto k diagnostic values you inquired about.
For a comprehensive understanding of this function, please visit the following link: https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM/blob/develop/R/R/extract_ic.R.

Please do not hesitate to reach out if you need further assistance.

Best,
Eunhwi

messages.subject: Bug report for hBayesDM
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
 gathered a set of data with attention set shifting (ASST) data, which is the rodent version of the Wisconsin card sorting test. I want to dive deeper into the psychological aspect of this data set, and I came across the hBayesDM package written in R. I think the Bayesian function in the hBayesDM package fits my needs. I want to adapt the wcs_sql.R function to fit ASST data. And rebuild a custom R package. But I found out that the Rstan is preventing the package building process and raised the following error: "Error in rstan::stanc(f, allow_undefined = TRUE, obfuscate_model_name = FALSE): parser failed badly; maybe try installing the V8 package"

I wonder if you have encountered a similar issue before. If so, could you please share how you solved it? I would appreciate your support.

I look forward to hearing from you!

Best regards!
Yueqing

We've noticed the error is usually due to any line including "#" (even in comments) in the stan file. You can replace "#"s with "//" to comment out lines.

Cheers,

messages.subject: Re: Bug report for hBayesDM
messages.body_plain:
Hi Yueqing,

More information on (1) what you have done and (2) what you need will be helpful to solve the issue.  Regarding the error message you shared, removing "#"s from all the stan files located within the '/hBayesDM/inst' folder (I guess you are referring to /hBayesDM/commons/stan_files <https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM/tree/develop/commons/stan_files>) might have caused the error. If you are trying to use the wcs_sqn model for your own dataset, I suggest you to make edits to the stan file (link <https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM/blob/develop/commons/stan_files/wcs_sql.stan>) with customized R codes. While doing this, make sure that your (new) stan file doesn't include "#" symbols to prevent the initial error you shared. Let me know if anything is unclear.

Cheers,
JH

Jeung-Hyun Lee
PhD candidate,
Computational Clinical Science Lab.
Department of Psychology
Seoul National University
Building 16, Room A107
Email : jhlee...@snu.ac.kr
Website : https://jeunghyunlee.github.io/

messages.subject: Bug Report: Error in is.null(data)
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am attempting to run a drift diffusion anaylsis using your package. However, I keep getting the error:

Error in is.null(data) || is.na <http://is.na>(data) :
  'length = 13407' in coercion to 'logical(1)'

This occurs when I execute this line of code:

output1 = choiceRT_ddm(data = df, niter = 2000, nwarmup = 1000, nchain = 4, ncore = 4)

I am using the attached data (although I am using the dataframe corresponding to the data- this is a .txt file with the dataframe info on it.)

Is there a way to resolve this issue? I am using the most recent version of R.

Thank you very much!
